drop.label: Drop
drop.hint: Click to place drops. Each click can be a different quantity and colour. Keys 1 to 9 pick a palette ink.

spray.label: Spray
spray.hint: Click, or drag, to spray fine dots. They use the colours chosen below.

fillDots.label: Fill dots
fillDots.hint: Fills the open space with dots, largest holes first. Use the button below.

text.label: Text
text.hint: Click to print the text as ink. It never grows, but rakes and drops move it.

paint.label: Paint
paint.hint: Drag to paint a line of ink. It doesn't spread, but later tools move it.

stripes.label: Stripes
stripes.hint: Fills the tank with bands of the palette's inks. Rake across them for chevrons. Use the button below.

rake.label: Rake
rake.hint: Drag across the tank: the rake travels along your line, teeth perpendicular to it.

hearts.label: Hearts
hearts.hint: A small tine through the middle of every dot that isn't frozen, which pulls them into hearts. Use the button below.

fullRake.label: Full rake
fullRake.hint: Teeth spread evenly across the whole page; offset slides them and wraps at the edges. Pick a direction, then use the button below.

stylus.label: Stylus
stylus.hint: Draw freely: a single tine follows your stroke.

jiggle.label: Jiggle
jiggle.hint: Shakes the whole tank into waves. Use the button below.

wriggle.label: Wriggle
wriggle.hint: Click a centre: rings around it twist back and forth.

stir.label: Stir
stir.hint: Click a centre: circular tines turn around it.

air.label: Air
air.hint: A breath of air across the whole tank. Each press is a different breath. Use the button below.

erase.label: Eraser
erase.hint: Click or drag to take ink away. Pause first to mark several spots, then play to watch them go.

options.drain: Ink and water: the surface closes up
options.lift: Just the ink: the water stays

vortex.label: Vortex
vortex.hint: Click a centre: a swirl spins up around it.

info.speed: How fast the simulation plays compared with real time. It doesn't change the result. Low framerate ignores this and runs as fast as it can.
info.finish: Skips ahead until everything has stopped moving.
info.profiling: Records where the time goes while the tank runs, every 2 seconds, to profiles/marbler-profile.jsonl next to this project. It stays on this computer. It holds timings and settings, not your scripts. Leave it off when you are not measuring something.
info.gridCell: How finely the Grid ink simulator divides the tank, in mm. Smaller is sharper and much slower: half the size is about four times the work. Takes effect the next time the tank clears.
info.simulator: Which physics moves the ink. Classic: the original; drops keep a fixed size and each pushes everything. Spreading: ink grows over bare water until it meets other ink. Thin film (beta): each ink can claim a limited area, which gives even rings. Film: ink carries pressure and water doesn't, so drops ignore each other until they touch. Best for filling the canvas. Wake: Film in a bath that keeps moving, so ink coasts and curls after a tool stops. Try viscosity 5 to 60. Wake (fast): the same simulation as Wake, but drawn in the background, so a busy tank keeps moving and the picture catches up. Prints and exports keep every point, and metallic ink only shows at rest. Grid ink (beta): ink is colour on a grid, moved by a full fluid solve, so colours blend softly and a flow never runs out of points. It repeats unless you untick Repeating, which gives it solid sides: ink stays in and the water turns back at the edge. It runs on the GPU.
info.walls: Keeps ink inside the rectangle, where it flattens against the walls. Off, ink pushed past the edge carries on out of view.
info.tile: Makes the tank one tile of a seamless repeat, joined at its edges like a torus: ink that leaves one side comes back in at the other. Exports join up when placed side by side. Only simulators that can repeat show this: Classic, Film, Wake and Grid ink. Grid ink starts out repeating. Turn doesn't work on a repeating tank. See it repeat shows four copies.
info.toolsWait: A rake or stir waits until all the ink has finished growing. Off, it starts straight away and catches drops mid-growth.
info.queueMode: What happens to things you add while paused: all start together, one after another with a gap, or each waiting for the last to settle.
info.lowFramerate: Shows a snapshot every 2 seconds or so instead of animating, and spends the time simulating, as fast as your computer allows. Good for heavy, beautiful runs. It switches on by itself when ticks get too slow, until the ink settles, and the status line then says "automatic". The page can feel sluggish while it works.
info.pull: Lays a sheet of paper across the tank, shows the print and keeps it in the Paper section.
info.pointLimit: Outlines are made of points, and stretched ink needs more of them to stay smooth. This is the most the tank will use. More keeps fine curls crisp but runs slower and uses more memory. Standard is tuned for smooth live play, and low framerate takes over when higher settings get slow. As a rough guide, each million points adds about 16 to 32 MB per copy, and undo keeps copies. Takes effect straight away.
info.flowPreset: How much life the bath has in the Wake simulator. Each preset also sets the viscosity. It takes effect straight away, on everything from here on, without clearing the tank. Higher settings make far more points. If the tank reaches the point limit, the bath stops so that the picture stays smooth, and a higher limit in Detail lets it run longer.
info.flowPush: How hard each tine shoves the water, as a multiple of normal. About 3 makes wakes roll up into whorls, and 10 is chaos.
info.flowFriction: Drag from the tank floor. Lower lets the water keep swirling for longer. Very thick baths add their own drag on top.
info.flowCoast: The longest the water keeps moving after a tool stops, whatever else is going on.
info.flowCell: The size of the boxes used to track how the water moves. Ink outlines stay sharp either way, but smaller boxes allow smaller curls. It matters most with high push and small tines, and halving it makes each tick about four times slower.
info.palette: A set of inks and a bath colour. Changing it recolours the swatches and the bath, not ink already in the tank.
info.myPalettes: Change colours and shimmer here, then type a name and press Save palette. It saves these inks with the Base colour from the top bar, and shows under My palettes. Scripts can use it with palette('its name'), and you can ask the assistant to save or switch palettes too. Built-in palettes never change. Saved palettes are kept in this browser only, so clearing its site data removes them.
info.assistant: Describe a pattern or a change and it edits the script below. Nothing happens in the tank until you press Run.
info.myScripts: Scripts you've kept, by name. Type a name and press Save script. Saving under a name you already used replaces that script, after asking. Choosing one opens it with the simulator it was saved on, ready to change. It doesn't run until you press Run, so your tank is safe. They're kept in this browser only, so clearing its site data removes them.
info.clearFirst: On, Run starts from an empty tank. Off, the script plays on top of the ink already there, starting now, and one Undo takes it all back. Its `at` times count from when it starts. Settings it changes, such as tile() or viscosity(), apply to the ink already there, and if the script fails, the tank goes back to how it was.
info.script: A JavaScript recipe for a whole design, so it can be repeated and shared. Positions and sizes are on a 0 to 100 page. Run plays it, clearing the tank first unless you untick that. Copy session writes what you've done by hand as a script.
info.savedStates: Keeps the tank exactly as it is now, in this browser, to come back to later. They survive a reload, but very big tanks may not fit in the browser's storage.
info.tankSize: The tank's size. Physics works in millimetres, so a bigger tank makes the same drop relatively smaller. Applying clears the tank.
info.viscosity: How thick the bath is, from 5 (thin as water) to 20000. It starts at 1000, or 200 for Grid ink, and changing simulator moves it to the new one's starting value unless you've typed your own. Lower generally means tines pull more. In Classic and Film, 200 pulls about five times as far and much lower can drag ink off the page. In Wake, 5 to 60 keeps the bath moving for seconds, giving curls. Changing it takes effect straight away, on everything from here on, without clearing the tank.
info.baseColour: A background colour under the ink. Off, an empty tank shows a faint grid, and exports have a transparent background. Print uses it as the paper colour.
info.imperfection: How imperfect a pull is: uneven pickup, grain, air bubbles and a hesitation line.
info.mirror: A real print is the tank's mirror image, so text reads backwards. Off, prints read the same way round as the tank.
info.pullBase: Pulls on paper in the tank's base colour, instead of the paper colour chosen here, so the print looks like the tank. It does nothing while Base colour is off.
info.clearAfter: Empties the tank once the paper has covered it.
info.autoSave: Downloads a PNG of each pull as well as keeping it in this browser.
info.exportButtons: PNG: exactly what the tank shows. SVG: scalable shapes in flat colour, without shimmer. Print: a slow 3000 pixel picture on paper with smooth curves. None of these change the tank.
info.printPale: Ink that spread further is a thinner layer, so it tints the paper less. It's a guess at real ink, kept subtle. Print only.
info.printTexture: Slightly deeper edges and uneven pigment. An artistic touch, not simulated. Print only.
info.printSoft: Lets inks bleed into each other in soft patches, so some edges stay crisp and others go hazy. It's a painterly effect added when printing, not simulated, and only Print shows it.
info.color.swatches: The inks of the current palette. Keys 1 to 9 pick them while this tool is chosen. The square at the end picks any colour.
info.color.alpha: How see-through the ink is. Overlaps between translucent inks can show seams in Film.
info.color.shimmer: Makes the ink metallic, with a moving glint. PNG and pulls include it; SVG and Print don't.
info.tool.drop: A drop of ink on the surface. How it spreads and what it pushes depends on the simulator.
info.tool.spray: A burst of very fine dots, mostly tiny and thickest in the middle, like flicking a brush.
info.tool.text: Prints letters as ink. They don't expand, but every later tool moves them, so they marble with everything else.
info.tool.paint: A brush for laying lines of ink. Unlike a drop it doesn't expand or push anything; it sits on top, then moves with everything else once you rake or stir.
info.tool.stripes: Covers the tank in bands of colour, the starting point for chevrons and bouquet patterns. Rake across the bands with Full rake, then back the other way with an offset. It adds to the tank rather than clearing it. The arrows set which way the bands run.
info.paint.taper: At 0 the line keeps its width. At 1 it narrows to a point at both ends, like a brush lifting.
info.paint.wobble: How far the line wanders from where you drew it, so it looks less mechanical.
info.stripes.count: How many bands. Many thin bands make fine, busy patterns once raked.
info.stripes.over: On top covers whatever is already in the tank. Around leaves that ink in sight, with the bands filling the rest. The bands really lie beneath it, so a rake moves both together.
info.stripes.variation: How uneven the bands are. At 0 they're equal and cycle through the palette in order. Higher mixes wide and narrow bands in random order.
info.stripes.wobble: How far the bands wander. At 0 they're dead straight.
info.stripes.slivers: Thin tapered streaks of another colour added per band, which make bands look hand-laid once combed.
info.tool.rake: A comb you drag by hand. Each tooth pulls ink along its path, which makes feathers and chevrons.
info.tool.fullRake: A comb across the whole page, for exact, repeatable passes. Two passes in opposite directions with an offset give classic combed patterns.
info.tool.stylus: A single tine that follows your hand, for drawing.
info.tool.jiggle: Shakes the whole tank in a wave, so straight lines become wavy.
info.tool.wriggle: Twists rings around a centre back and forth, leaving a rippled, turbulent look, especially in Wake.
info.tool.stir: Circular tines turning around a centre, which winds ink into spirals.
info.tool.air: A breath of air over the whole bath: a smooth random flow that stretches and swirls the ink without changing its area. Scripts can pass a seed to repeat the same breath. In Wake it also sets the bath moving.
info.air.scale: How big the swirls are. A second breath at a smaller size adds fine turbulence on top.
info.air.speed: How fast the air moves the ink, and so how far the ink gets pushed.
info.air.octaves: How many layers of smaller swirls are added to the main ones.
info.tool.fillDots: Packs the tank with dots of many sizes, biggest holes first, each in the palette's inks with neighbours avoiding a match. It goes around ink already there unless you tell it to go on top. Press it again to fill what's left.
info.tool.erase: Takes ink away, either letting the surface close over the hole or leaving bare water. Not available in Grid ink yet.
info.fillDots.count: The most dots it will place. It stops sooner if no hole is left that's big enough.
info.fillDots.min: The smallest dot it will place. Lower it to fill the little gaps between the big dots.
info.fillDots.max: The largest dot, which goes in the biggest hole first.
info.fillDots.gap: Clear space kept between dots. They spread and touch less with more of it.
info.fillDots.tightness: How fully a dot fills its hole. Lower varies the sizes more, and higher packs them closer.
info.fillDots.rings: Colours stacked in each dot, like a target. Each layer waits for the one before to settle.
info.fillDots.sprayColors: Use every ink in the palette, or just the one chosen above.
info.fillDots.over: Dots normally go in the open space around ink already there. On top lets them land anywhere.
info.erase.mode: Ink and water drains everything inside the circle to its centre, and the surface around slides in to close the hole. Just the ink cuts the ink out at once and leaves bare water, with everything else staying where it is.
info.erase.radius: How much ink it takes away. The area lost is exactly this circle's.
info.erase.duration: How long the ink takes to drain and the surface to close. Just the ink happens at once.
info.tileOffset: How the repeat lines up. None stacks the tiles straight. Brick shifts each row of tiles by half a tile, like a brick wall, and half-drop shifts each column, like a lot of printed wallpaper. See it repeat shows the result. Not in Grid ink yet.
info.tool.vortex: A swirl that spins up around a point and fades with distance.
info.drop.quantity: How much ink, and so how big the drop ends up. In Film and Spreading, a drop on open water grows further than one landing on ink.
info.drop.dispersion: How quickly a drop reaches its full size. It doesn't change the final size.
info.drop.count: How many drops each click places, using Scatter to spread them.
info.drop.scatter: How far from your click the drops can land.
info.spray.sprayColors: Use every ink in the palette at random, or only the chosen one.
info.spray.n: How many dots each burst makes. Dragging adds bursts as you go.
info.spray.min: The size of the tiniest dots.
info.spray.max: The size of the largest dots. Most dots stay close to the smallest size.
info.rake.waveShape: The path each tooth follows as it travels. Straight goes in a line; the others swing side to side in that shape. Needs some weave height to show.
info.rake.teeth: How many teeth the rake has.
info.rake.speed: How fast the tool travels. It changes how much ink gets pulled as well as how long the stroke takes: faster reaches further. In Wake, a fast tool also leaves more movement in the bath.
info.rake.D: How far the pull reaches. Ink nearby gets carried along, more so the higher this is, though the tine itself stays a point. Very high values drag the whole page along, so a full-width rake can push all the ink off an open tank. In Wake, more thickness stops adding direct pull fairly early.
info.rake.width: The physical size of each tine. Ink bulges aside and closes up behind it, instead of being dragged. If the width is more than about twice the pull's reach, you only get the bulge.
info.rake.waveAmp: How far each tooth swings to the side. Overlapping neighbouring teeth is fine and often the point.
info.rake.waveLength: How far the rake travels for one full swing of the weave. Short gives tight, busy marks.
info.fullRake.waveShape: The path each tooth follows as it travels. Straight goes in a line; the others swing side to side in that shape. Needs some weave height to show.
info.fullRake.angle: The direction the rake travels: 0 is right, 90 up, 180 left, 270 down, and anything between runs at a slant. The arrows above jump to those four. On a repeating tank it runs at the nearest angle where the teeth join back up with themselves, and says so.
info.tool.hearts: Drags one small tine through the middle of every loop, the classic way to turn dots into hearts. It leaves frozen ink alone, and the rings of a target count as one dot. The dashed lines show where each tine will run. Not available in Grid ink.
info.hearts.angle: The way the tines travel, which is the way the points face. 270 is down.
info.hearts.above: Where each tine starts, measured from the middle of its dot: 0 is the middle, 100 is the edge, and more is outside the dot.
info.hearts.below: Where each tine ends, measured the same way. Going past the edge draws out the point.
info.hearts.pull: How widely each tine pulls, as a percentage of its own dot's radius, so big and small dots get the same shape.
info.hearts.min: Dots smaller than this are left alone. The dashed lines show which dots it will rake.
info.hearts.max: Dots larger than this are left alone. All the way up reaches even a dot as big as the tank.
info.hearts.speed: How fast the tines travel. Small dots finish first.
info.freeze: Holds chosen ink still, like a mask. Choose Freeze and click any ink, or Unfreeze and click it to let it go, and Clear all to let everything go. Frozen ink shows in red while Full rake is open, and with a dashed outline in other tools. Nothing moves it, whichever tool you use, and raked ink passes underneath it. Not available in Grid ink.
info.fullRake.teeth: How many teeth the rake has. They spread evenly across the page.
info.fullRake.offset: Slides all the teeth sideways, wrapping at the edges. A second pass with half a tooth's offset lands between the first pass's lines.
info.fullRake.speed: How fast the tool travels. It changes how much ink gets pulled as well as how long the stroke takes: faster reaches further. In Wake, a fast tool also leaves more movement in the bath.
info.fullRake.D: How far the pull reaches. Ink nearby gets carried along, more so the higher this is, though the tine itself stays a point. Very high values drag the whole page along, so a full-width rake can push all the ink off an open tank. In Wake, more thickness stops adding direct pull fairly early.
info.fullRake.width: The physical size of each tine. Ink bulges aside and closes up behind it, instead of being dragged. If the width is more than about twice the pull's reach, you only get the bulge.
info.fullRake.waveAmp: How far each tooth swings to the side. Overlapping neighbouring teeth is fine and often the point.
info.fullRake.waveLength: How far the rake travels for one full swing of the weave. Short gives tight, busy marks.
info.stylus.speed: How fast the tool travels. It changes how much ink gets pulled as well as how long the stroke takes: faster reaches further. In Wake, a fast tool also leaves more movement in the bath.
info.stylus.D: How far the pull reaches. Ink nearby gets carried along, more so the higher this is, though the tine itself stays a point. Very high values drag the whole page along, so a full-width rake can push all the ink off an open tank. In Wake, more thickness stops adding direct pull fairly early.
info.stylus.width: The physical size of each tine. Ink bulges aside and closes up behind it, instead of being dragged. If the width is more than about twice the pull's reach, you only get the bulge.
info.jiggle.angle: The direction the wave travels in.
info.jiggle.period: The distance from one wave crest to the next.
info.jiggle.amplitude: How far the ink moves to each side.
info.wriggle.direction: Which way the rings turn first.
info.wriggle.period: The distance between rings that twist in opposite directions.
info.stir.direction: The way the rings turn. Alternating gives each ring the opposite direction to the last.
info.stir.rings: How many circular tines there are.
info.stir.degrees: How far the rings turn in total.
info.stir.D: How far each ring's pull reaches.
info.vortex.circulation: How strongly it spins. Ink nearest the centre moves most.

simulators.label: Classic
simulators.title: The original: drops keep a fixed size and each one pushes everything, water included.

simulators.label: Spreading
simulators.title: Ink spreads over bare water until it meets other ink.

simulators.label: Thin film (beta)
simulators.title: Tracks how much surface each ink can still claim. Bare water has no pressure, so films only feel each other once they touch.

simulators.label: Film
simulators.title: Ink is a film that carries pressure and water is not. Films ignore each other until they touch, then push as one.

simulators.label: Wake
simulators.title: Film, in a bath that keeps moving. Tools leave a flow that lasts longer the thinner the bath is, with curls and wobble behind fast rakes. Try viscosity 5 to 60.

simulators.label: Wake (fast)
simulators.title: The same simulation as Wake, but drawn in the background with outlines thinned to what the screen can show, so busy tanks keep moving. Prints and exports keep every point.

simulators.label: Grid ink (beta)
simulators.title: Ink is colour on a grid, moved by a full fluid solve (BiMocq2), so it blends softly and flows can run as long as you like. Repeats unless you turn that off, which gives it solid sides. Runs on the GPU where it can.
